transcript.text: Every time I put the oven on it runs for a few minutes and then the trip switch goes and half the house loses power. Reset it 3 times tonight. Hotpoint built-in, about 9 years old. What could cause this?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the oven switched off at its cooker switch (isolator) or at the fuse box and don't use it until it has been checked — never test it with the power on. One detail helps the engineer: does it trip as soon as it is switched on, or only after it has been heating for a while (or only on one function)?

It doesn't trip as soon as it's switched on - it trips about 2 to 5 minutes into heating with the fan oven. I did once run just the grill for 10 minutes and that didn't trip it. I'll leave it off now.

Thanks for letting us know about the tripping issue. Moisture is a common trigger for this problem. Please switch the oven off at the wall or its cooker switch (isolator) and let it cool completely first. Has the oven been cleaned recently with oven cleaner, steam or a lot of water, or got wet in any way?

Yes, I cleaned the inside of the oven with oven spray the weekend before this started. I haven't seen any other water or spillage. I've switched it off at the cooker switch and the trip hasn't gone since.

[Heading: Moisture in an element after cleaning]
Thanks for letting me know about the recent cleaning. Keep it switched off at the cooker switch until then and don't keep resetting the trip. I'm not recommending a part from this.
You said to keep it off "until then", but until when? Should I get an engineer in, and what should I do next?

[Heading: Moisture in an element after cleaning]
No problem at all, nothing changes from what I said above. An appliance engineer is the best next step to confirm it safely. Please note that I am not recommending a specific part in this instance. Given your Hotpoint oven cooker trips after heating on one function and was recently cleaned while wet, professional assessment is required.
